raw.details:
Overview

THREWS ODYSSEY 2026 is an online research and innovation hackathon organised by Threws – The Research World.

The hackathon brings together students, developers, researchers and technology enthusiasts to build practical solutions to real-world problems across multiple domains.

Participants can choose a problem from one of the following tracks:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
  • Medical & HealthTech
  • Cybersecurity
  • FinTech
  • ClimateTech & Sustainability
  • DeepTech & Scientific Computing
  • Smart Cities & Social Impact
  • Human-AI & Assistive Technology
  • Web3, Privacy & Decentralised Systems
  • Open Innovation

What to Build

Participants are expected to identify a meaningful problem and develop a working solution. Projects can be software products, AI/ML systems, research prototypes, cybersecurity solutions, data-driven applications or other technology-based solutions relevant to the selected track.

Projects should demonstrate a clear problem statement, a well-defined approach and a functional prototype. Participants are encouraged to research existing solutions and explain how their approach improves upon or differs from them.

Eligibility

  • Open to college students, freshers, professionals, researchers and independent developers.
  • Participants from any academic or technical background can apply.
  • Participation is open to individuals as well as teams.
  • Maximum team size: 2 members.
  • Participants may choose any one of the available tracks.

Hackathon Process

  • Register for THREWS ODYSSEY 2026.
  • Select a track and identify a problem.
  • Develop the solution during the hackathon period.
  • Test and refine the project.
  • Submit the project before the submission deadline.
  • Submissions will be reviewed by the judging panel.
  • Shortlisted participants may be invited for a final demonstration or presentation.
  • Winners will be announced after the final evaluation.

Submission Requirements

Each submission must include:

  • Project name
  • Problem statement
  • Description of the proposed solution
  • Key features
  • Technology stack
  • Source code / repository
  • Working prototype or demonstration
  • Brief explanation of the implementation
  • Dataset and external resources used, where applicable
  • Results or evaluation, where applicable

A short demo video may also be requested for shortlisted projects.

Judging

Projects will be evaluated on:

  • Innovation and originality
  • Technical implementation
  • Relevance and importance of the problem
  • Quality of the solution
  • Research, experimentation and use of data where applicable
  • Potential impact and scalability
  • Quality of the final demonstration

Rules

  • Submissions must be the original work of the participating individual or team.
  • Pre-existing projects may be used as a starting point only if substantial new work is carried out during the hackathon and clearly disclosed.
  • Participants may use open-source libraries, APIs, datasets and development tools, subject to their respective licences.
  • Use of AI coding and research tools is permitted. Participants must understand the work submitted under their name and be able to explain it during evaluation.
  • All third-party resources must be properly acknowledged.
  • Plagiarism, copied submissions, fabricated results or misrepresentation of work may result in disqualification.
  • Each participant may be part of only one team.
  • Projects must comply with applicable laws, licences and ethical standards.
  • The organisers reserve the right to reject submissions that do not meet the eligibility or submission requirements.
  • The decision of the judging panel will be final.

The objective of THREWS ODYSSEY is simple: find meaningful problems, explore better solutions and build something that can make a difference.

Build something worth discovering.

Prizes & Recognition

Total Prize Pool: ₹1,50,000
